Headline: JPMorgan Chase becomes the new issuer of the Apple Card
Summary: JPMorgan Chase has become the new issuer of the Apple Card, replacing Goldman Sachs, with the transition expected to take up to 24 months. The deal is projected to bring over $20 billion in card balances to Chase, although Goldman Sachs will offload this amount at a $1 billion discount. The Apple Card will continue to operate on the Mastercard network, and current users will not experience any immediate changes.

Headline: Waymo is rebranding its Zeekr robotaxi
Summary: Waymo is rebranding its Zeekr robotaxi to Ojai, named after a village in California, as it prepares for its commercial launch. The decision to change the name stems from the U.S. public's unfamiliarity with the Zeekr brand, and the Ojai will greet passengers with a personalized message. The vehicle has undergone refinements and is set to expand Waymo's robotaxi service, which currently operates in several U.S. cities, with plans to launch in more locations soon.

Headline: Ford has an AI assistant and new hands-free BlueCruise tech on the way
Summary: Ford is set to launch an AI assistant integrated into its smartphone app in early 2026, with plans for in-vehicle deployment in 2027. Additionally, the company announced a next-generation BlueCruise advanced driver assistance system that will be 30% cheaper to produce and aims to enable eyes-off driving by 2028.

Headline: Yes, LinkedIn banned AI agent startup Artisan, but now it’s back
Summary: Artisan AI, a startup specializing in AI agents for outbound sales, was recently banned from LinkedIn due to concerns over data scraping and unauthorized use of the platform's name. After addressing these issues, the company has been reinstated on LinkedIn, highlighting the scrutiny that AI companies face regarding data usage. The incident serves as a cautionary tale for startups in the AI space, indicating that major platforms are vigilant about compliance with their policies.

Headline: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Health, says 230 million users ask about health each week
Summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Health, a dedicated platform for users to discuss health-related topics, responding to the fact that over 230 million users inquire about health each week. The new feature aims to separate health conversations from general chats and will integrate with personal health data from wellness apps, while emphasizing that it is not intended for diagnosing or treating health conditions.

Headline: Lux Capital lands $1.5B for its largest fund ever
Summary: Lux Capital has successfully closed a $1.5 billion ninth fund, marking the largest fund in the firm's history. This fundraising comes amid a challenging environment for venture capital, with 2025 seeing a 10-year low in new VC funds raised in the U.S. The firm has a strong track record in defense technology and AI investments, contributing to its appeal among limited partners.

Headline: Anthropic reportedly raising $10B at $350B valuation
Summary: Anthropic is reportedly raising $10 billion at a $350 billion valuation, with Coatue Management and Singapore’s GIC leading the funding round. This new raise follows a previous $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation just three months ago, nearly doubling the company's value. The fresh capital comes as Anthropic prepares for a potential IPO this year, alongside its competitor OpenAI.

Headline: How Quilt solved the heat pump’s biggest challenge
Summary: Smart home startup Quilt has launched a three-zone heat pump that maintains efficiency in challenging conditions, addressing a significant limitation of traditional systems. The company has leveraged data from its existing units to optimize performance, allowing the new unit to deliver nearly 90% of its rated capacity at extremely low temperatures. Recently, Quilt secured a $20 million Series B funding round to support its expansion plans.

Headline: Trump suddenly sounds a lot like a progressive Democrat when it comes to business
Summary: Former President Donald Trump has threatened to ban institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, a stance that aligns him more closely with progressive Democrats' concerns about housing affordability and market manipulation. This unexpected position highlights a shift in his rhetoric regarding business practices and the impact of large investors on the housing market.

Headline: Trump threatens to ban institutional investors from buying single-family homes
Summary: Former President Donald Trump has threatened to ban institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, citing concerns over housing affordability and the impact of large-scale investors on the housing market. This move could significantly affect the dynamics of home buying and investment strategies in the residential real estate sector.

Headline: Meta faces China probe over acquisition of AI agent startup Manus
Summary: Meta is under investigation by China's Ministry of Commerce regarding its $2 billion acquisition of AI startup Manus, which aims to enhance automation in its products. The probe will assess compliance with export control laws and regulations related to technology imports and overseas investments. Manus, previously a product of a Chinese startup, relocated to Singapore earlier this year and has been recognized for its AI capabilities.

Headline: Magnificent Seven competition heats up
Summary: The article discusses the competitive landscape among the "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks, highlighting Alphabet's rise to a market capitalization of $3.89 trillion, surpassing Apple's $3.85 trillion for the first time since 2019. This shift reflects Apple's struggles in the AI sector, particularly with delays in launching an upgraded Siri, while Alphabet's rapid deployment of AI models has bolstered its performance. Additionally, Tesla and Nvidia are making strides in AI for self-driving vehicles, as Nvidia's CEO announced a new AI reasoning model at the CES conference.

Headline: The first of China’s 'AI tigers' goes public as Zhipu climbs in Hong Kong debut
Summary: Zhipu, a major Chinese AI startup, made its public debut in Hong Kong with an initial public offering (IPO) that raised $558 million, marking it as the first of China's "AI tigers" to go public. The stock rose as much as 15% above its offer price of 116.20 Hong Kong Dollars ($15), valuing the company at approximately HK$4.3 billion. Zhipu aims to compete with American AI giants like OpenAI, despite facing challenges due to U.S. restrictions.

Headline: Samsung Electronics estimates nearly three-fold profit surge as memory prices skyrocket
Summary: Samsung Electronics expects a nearly three-fold increase in operating profit for Q4 2025, projecting 20 trillion won, driven by a surge in memory prices, which rose 40%-50% due to high demand from AI applications. This profit forecast surpasses Samsung's previous record of 17.6 trillion won set in 2018, although the company still lags behind SK Hynix in high-bandwidth memory production critical for AI chips.

Headline: Microsoft revealed as company behind controversial data center proposal in Michigan
Summary: Microsoft has been identified as the company behind a controversial data center proposal in Lowell Charter Township, Michigan, where local residents have expressed concerns about the project's rapid progression and its energy requirements. The announcement follows a postponed public hearing due to community pushback, with Microsoft stating its intention to provide more information and transparency regarding the proposal.

Headline: The boldest bitcoin predictions for 2026 are in — from $75,000 to $225,000
Summary: Industry executives and investors predict that bitcoin could range between $75,000 and $225,000 in 2026, following a year of significant volatility. Factors such as lower interest rates and a more favorable regulatory environment in the U.S. are expected to influence its price, despite a challenging backdrop characterized by geopolitical uncertainties and stretched equity valuations.

Headline: Google, Character.AI to settle suits involving minor suicides and AI chatbots
Summary: Google and Character.AI have reached a settlement with families who sued them over psychological harm to minors, including cases linked to suicides allegedly caused by AI chatbots. The lawsuits claimed negligence and wrongful death, with one notable case involving a 14-year-old boy whose interactions with a chatbot were cited as harmful. Settlement details are still being finalized, and the companies are now tasked with addressing the potential dangers associated with their technology.

Headline: Alphabet's market cap surpasses Apple’s for first time since 2019
Summary: Alphabet's market capitalization has surpassed Apple's for the first time since 2019, closing at $3.88 trillion compared to Apple's $3.84 trillion. This shift highlights the differing strategies of the two companies in artificial intelligence, with Alphabet experiencing a significant 65% stock increase in 2025, driven by advancements in AI technology and a strong performance in its cloud business.

Headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Health to connect user medical records, wellness apps
Summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Health, a feature that allows users to securely connect their medical records and wellness apps to the chatbot, enhancing its ability to provide personalized responses. The service is not intended for diagnosis or treatment and will not use conversations for training its models, ensuring user privacy. OpenAI has partnered with b.well to facilitate health data connectivity, allowing integration with various health and wellness applications.

Headline: Anthropic signs term sheet for $10 billion round at $350 billion valuation
Summary: Anthropic has signed a term sheet for a $10 billion funding round at a valuation of $350 billion, with Coatue and the Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC leading the financing. The company, founded by former OpenAI executives, is known for its Claude family of large language models and is competing against rivals like OpenAI, which has a valuation of $500 billion.

Headline: Tesla CEO Musk brushes off Nvidia self-driving competition as 5 or 6 years away
Summary: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, stated that it will take several years before Nvidia's new autonomous vehicle models can compete with Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology, suggesting a timeline of 5 to 6 years. This comment follows Nvidia's announcement of Alpamayo, a family of AI models for autonomous vehicle development, during the CES conference in Las Vegas. Musk emphasized that legacy car manufacturers will also lag in integrating the necessary technology at scale.

Headline: eVTOL maker Joby buys new factory, more than doubling manufacturing footprint
Summary: Joby Aviation has purchased a 700,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Dayton, Ohio, for $61.5 million, significantly expanding its manufacturing footprint as it aims to double production capacity to four aircraft per month by 2027. This facility marks Joby's third manufacturing site and is part of its strategy to meet the growing demand for electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft (eVTOLs) while pursuing FAA certification for commercial operations.

Headline: Memory chip giants spark global semiconductor rally as shortages stoke price hikes
Summary: Samsung Electronics anticipates a nearly three-fold increase in operating profit, projecting 20 trillion won for Q4 2025, driven by a 40%-50% surge in memory prices amid high demand for AI applications. This profit forecast surpasses its previous record of 17.6 trillion won set in 2018, highlighting a significant shift in the memory market dynamics as companies like Nvidia compete for limited supplies.

Headline: Turing Quantum completes hundreds of millions in strategic financing
Summary: Turing Quantum has completed a strategic financing round amounting to hundreds of millions of yuan, with participation from national-level capital and market institutions including Dinghui Baifu, Guoke Capital, Haitong Kaiyuan, and Jianggen Capital. The funds will be used to further research and industrialize photonic quantum computing, contributing to the development of the quantum computing ecosystem. This marks the second financing round for Turing Quantum within six months.

Headline: Rui Shi Elderly Care secures seed round financing to accelerate market expansion in Southwest
Summary: Rui Shi Elderly Care, a company focused on providing standardized bathing services for the elderly, has secured seed round financing from Pengbo Investment, achieving a post-investment valuation of several million RMB. The funding will be used to enhance its offline service network and team, as well as to accelerate the development of its proprietary management system and patented technology, aiming to expand its market presence in Southwest China.

Headline: Gai Lik Si, the first batch of GEO service providers in China, completes $10 million angel round financing
Summary: Gai Lik Si, a pioneering GEO service provider in China, has successfully completed a $10 million angel round financing, led by American investor PrinceX. The funding will be utilized to accelerate the development of GEO technology, enhance product offerings, and expand market reach, positioning the company to capitalize on the growing demand for AI-driven localized decision-making solutions.

Headline: Qiang Brain Technology: Completed 2 billion yuan financing
Summary: Qiang Brain Technology has successfully completed a financing round of 2 billion yuan, marking the second-largest funding record in the brain-computer interface sector globally, following Elon Musk's Neuralink. The funds will be utilized to accelerate the development of core technologies, engineering breakthroughs, and the mass production of their products.

Headline: Semafor, a US digital media startup, completes $30 million financing
Summary: Semafor, a U.S. digital media startup, has completed a $30 million financing round, bringing its valuation to $330 million. The company was founded in 2022 by former Bloomberg Media CEO Justin B. Smith and former Buzzfeed editor Ben Smith.

Headline: Zhi Zhan Technology completes nearly 300 million yuan Series C financing
Summary: Zhi Zhan Technology has completed nearly 300 million yuan in Series C financing, attracting investments from multiple firms including Tongxin Capital and Huaying Capital. The company focuses on silicon carbide wide bandgap semiconductors and advanced power conversion technologies, with plans to enhance its market share in the electric vehicle sector and expand into intelligent control markets following this funding round.

Headline: AI company Clipto.AI announces completion of a new round of Pre-A++ financing
Summary: AI company Clipto.AI has completed a new round of Pre-A++ financing, raising funds that have pushed its post-financing valuation to over $250 million. The round was led by EnvisionX Capital and Palm Drive Capital, with participation from existing investors including Sequoia China and GL Ventures, and will primarily be used to enhance research and development in multimodal AI models and system architecture.

Headline: The most bizarre tech announced so far at CES 2026
Summary: The article highlights some of the most unusual tech products unveiled at CES 2026, including Razer's animated holographic desk companion, an AI-powered panda robot for elderly care, and a musical lollipop that plays music through bone conduction. Other quirky gadgets featured include a $500 AI ice maker and a vibrating chef's knife priced at $399, showcasing the event's blend of innovation and eccentricity in consumer technology.

Headline: CES 2026: Follow live for the best, weirdest, and most interesting tech as physical AI and robots dominate the event
Summary: CES 2026 is currently underway in Las Vegas, showcasing a range of innovative technologies, particularly in AI and robotics. Highlights include LG's AI-powered home robot CLOid, designed to assist with household chores, and Vocci's new note-taking ring that offers significant recording capabilities. The event continues to attract attention with various tech reveals and discussions on advancements in autonomous vehicles and gaming devices.

Headline: Illinois health department exposed over 700,000 residents’ personal data for years
Summary: The Illinois Department of Human Services has confirmed a security lapse that exposed the personal information of over 700,000 residents for nearly four years, from April 2021 to September 2025. The exposed data includes details of Medicaid and Medicare Savings Program recipients, as well as individuals receiving services from the Division of Rehabilitation Services, although names were not included. Officials are currently unable to determine if the data was accessed during this period.

Headline: Why this VC thinks 2026 will be ‘the year of the consumer’
Summary: Vanessa Larco, a VC partner at Premise, predicts that 2026 will be "the year of the consumer," as consumer tech is poised for a resurgence after a downturn since 2022. She emphasizes that consumer adoption of AI products is quicker and more straightforward than in enterprise settings, and she anticipates new monetization strategies and business models will emerge as consumer experiences evolve online.

Headline: PhotonPay completes tens of millions of dollars in Series B financing, led by IDG Capital
Summary: PhotonPay, a global AI-driven digital financial infrastructure platform, has successfully completed a Series B financing round, raising tens of millions of dollars, led by IDG Capital with participation from several other investors. The company aims to address the complexities of global payment systems by building an independent financial infrastructure that simplifies cross-border transactions for businesses, reducing costs and enhancing efficiency.

Headline: Zhileng Low Temperature completes 70 million yuan financing
Summary: Zhileng Low Temperature has successfully completed a financing round of 70 million yuan, with participation from Anhui Guoyao Seed Fund, managed by Guoyao Capital. Summary: Zhileng Low Temperature, a high-tech company specializing in ultra-low temperature dilution refrigeration equipment, has completed a financing round of 70 million yuan. Headline: Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI will face a jury in March
Summary: Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI is set to go to trial in March after a U.S. judge found evidence supporting Musk's claims that OpenAI and its co-founders violated their original agreements by prioritizing profit over their nonprofit mission. Musk, who invested approximately $38 million in OpenAI, is seeking damages for what he describes as "ill-gotten gains" from the company's transition to a for-profit model. OpenAI has dismissed the lawsuit as baseless, characterizing it as part of Musk's ongoing harassment.

Headline: Google moonshot spinout SandboxAQ claims an ex-exec is attempting ‘extortion’
Summary: SandboxAQ, a Google moonshot spinout, is facing a wrongful termination lawsuit from former Chief of Staff Robert Bender, who alleges misconduct by CEO Jack Hidary, including misuse of company resources and misleading financial information to investors. SandboxAQ has denied the allegations, labeling Bender a "serial liar" and claiming the lawsuit is an attempt at extortion. The case highlights internal issues within the company and raises questions about corporate governance in Silicon Valley.

Headline: The venture firm that ate Silicon Valley just raised another $15 billion
Summary: Andreessen Horowitz has raised over $15 billion in new funding, bringing its total assets under management to more than $90 billion, making it one of the largest venture firms globally. The new capital will be allocated across various funds, including significant investments in growth, apps, infrastructure, and a focus on "American Dynamism," which aligns with U.S. defense priorities. The firm has also made substantial bets in the AI sector, positioning itself across the entire AI stack.

Headline: OpenAI is reportedly asking contractors to upload real work from past jobs
Summary: OpenAI is reportedly asking contractors to upload examples of real work from their past jobs as part of a strategy to generate high-quality training data for AI models. This approach raises concerns about the potential risks associated with handling proprietary and confidential information, as contractors are instructed to delete sensitive data before submission.

Headline: Google co-founders may be leaving California
Summary: Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page are reportedly reducing their presence in California, with multiple limited liability companies associated with them either being terminated or moved to Nevada. This shift appears to be a strategic move to avoid a potential 5% tax on billionaires that could be imposed if a ballot measure passes later this year.

Headline: Huaxin Micro-Nano Completes Series A Financing
Summary: Huaxin Micro-Nano has successfully completed its Series A financing, although the amount raised has not been disclosed. The investment round included participation from several institutions, such as Anhui High-tech Investment and China National New Holding, and positions Huaxin Micro-Nano as a leading 8-inch MEMS wafer foundry in China, focusing on various MEMS manufacturing applications.

Headline: ByteDance, Meituan, and Alibaba Bet Together as Zivariable Completes 1 Billion Yuan A++ Round Financing
Summary: Zivariable has successfully completed a 1 billion yuan A++ round of financing, with investments from major firms including ByteDance, Meituan, and Alibaba, making it the only embodied intelligence company in China to receive backing from all three tech giants. This round also marks the first investment from the Shenzhen Capital Group's AI fund since its establishment.

Headline: More than 100 new tech unicorns were minted in 2025 — here they are
Summary: In 2025, over 100 new tech unicorns emerged, primarily driven by a surge in AI-related startups, alongside notable entrants in sectors like satellite technology and blockchain. The article highlights several startups that achieved unicorn status, including Unconventional AI, valued at $4.5 billion, and Erebor, a crypto bank valued at $4.3 billion, reflecting a diverse landscape of innovation and investment in the tech industry.

Headline: China Mobile Chain Long Fund strategically supports the domestic first atomic quantum computing system R&D team, completing a new round of strategic financing
Summary: China's Zhongke Kuyan Technology has secured nearly 100 million yuan in strategic financing from China Mobile Chain Long Fund to accelerate the development of its atomic quantum computing system. This funding will support hardware research, new product iterations, and application exploration, positioning the company as a leader in the domestic quantum technology sector.

Headline: More than 100 new tech unicorns were minted in 2025 — here they are
Summary: In 2025, over 100 new tech unicorns emerged, driven largely by advancements in AI, with notable entries from various sectors including aerospace and blockchain. The article highlights several startups that achieved unicorn status, such as Unconventional AI, valued at $4.5 billion, and Erebor, a crypto bank valued at $4.3 billion, showcasing a diverse range of innovative companies. The list will be updated throughout the year to reflect new additions to the unicorn club.

Headline: OpenAI buys tiny health records startup Torch for, reportedly, $100M
Summary: OpenAI has acquired the health records startup Torch for a reported $100 million. Torch, which consists of a four-person team, developed technology to unify medical information from various sources into a single context engine, and will now contribute to OpenAI's newly launched ChatGPT Health service.

Headline: Hands-on with Bee, Amazon’s latest AI wearable
Summary: Amazon's latest AI wearable, Bee, offers a user-friendly experience for recording and transcribing conversations, segmenting audio into summarized sections. However, it raises concerns about privacy and social norms regarding recording conversations in public, as it is not always listening by default and requires user consent to record. The device's success will depend on consumer acceptance of such technology in everyday life.

Headline: Why Amazon bought Bee, an AI wearable
Summary: Amazon has acquired Bee, an AI wearable device designed for recording conversations and serving as an AI companion, to expand its presence in the consumer AI market beyond home devices like Alexa. Bee's capabilities include learning from user interactions and providing personalized insights, positioning it as a complementary tool to Alexa, with potential future integration between the two technologies.

Headline: Mark Zuckerberg says Meta is launching its own AI infrastructure initiative
Summary: Mark Zuckerberg announced that Meta is launching a new initiative called Meta Compute to enhance its AI infrastructure, aiming to significantly expand its energy capacity over the next decade. The company plans to build tens of gigawatts of energy capacity, which is crucial for supporting its AI business and maintaining a competitive edge in the rapidly evolving tech landscape.

Headline: Anthropic announces Claude for Healthcare following OpenAI’s ChatGPT Health reveal
Summary: Anthropic has launched Claude for Healthcare, a new set of tools designed for healthcare providers, payers, and patients, following OpenAI's introduction of ChatGPT Health. Claude aims to enhance efficiency in healthcare processes, such as prior authorization reviews, by integrating with various health data platforms, while addressing concerns about the reliability of AI-generated medical advice.

Headline: Pebble founder says his new company is ‘not a startup’
Summary: Eric Migicovsky, the founder of Pebble, has launched a new company called Core Devices, which he emphasizes is "not a startup." The company focuses on sustainable and profitable practices, offering a reboot of the Pebble smartwatch brand and an AI ring, with a small team and no outside funding. Migicovsky aims to create products for a niche audience, prioritizing a limited vision over broad market appeal.

Headline: Anthropic’s new Cowork tool offers Claude Code without the code
Summary: Anthropic has launched a new tool called Cowork, designed to make its Claude Code more accessible by allowing users to designate a folder for Claude to read or modify files through a chat interface. Currently in research preview and available only to Max subscribers, Cowork aims to facilitate non-coding tasks while warning users about potential risks associated with vague instructions.

Headline: Trump’s EPA plans to ignore health effects of air pollution
Summary: The Trump administration's Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to disregard the health impacts of air pollution when regulating ozone and fine particulate matter, a significant departure from decades of practice that valued human life in cost-benefit analyses. This policy change comes amid increasing reliance on polluting energy sources and has been welcomed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, which views it as a move towards more balanced regulations.

Headline: Amazon says 97% of its devices can support Alexa+
Summary: Amazon announced that 97% of its devices can support its new AI assistant, Alexa+, which aims to enhance user experience with more expressive voices and task-performing capabilities. With over 600 million devices sold, Amazon is focusing on rolling out Alexa+ to Prime members first, leveraging its existing customer base to compete in the generative AI market.

Headline: Fintech firm Betterment confirms data breach after hackers send fake crypto scam notification to users
Summary: Fintech firm Betterment has confirmed a data breach that occurred on January 9, where hackers accessed personal information of some customers through a social engineering attack. The breach allowed the attackers to send fraudulent notifications to users, but Betterment stated that no customer accounts or login credentials were compromised. The company is conducting an ongoing investigation with the help of a cybersecurity firm.

Headline: Developers have made $550B on Apple’s App Store since 2008
Summary: Developers have earned $550 billion from Apple's App Store since its launch in 2008, reflecting significant growth from the $260 billion reported in 2021. In 2025, Apple also reported 850 million average weekly App Store users and record highs in Apple Music listenership and new subscribers, amidst ongoing scrutiny over its commission practices.

Headline: Google’s Gemini to power Apple’s AI features like Siri
Summary: Apple has partnered with Google to utilize its Gemini AI technology for enhancing features like Siri, reportedly for around $1 billion. This multi-year agreement follows Apple's exploration of other AI technologies and aims to improve Siri's capabilities while maintaining the company's focus on user privacy. The partnership comes amid ongoing antitrust scrutiny of Google, particularly regarding its default search agreements with Apple.

Headline: Paramount files lawsuit against Warner Bros. amidst controversial Netflix merger
Summary: Paramount has filed a lawsuit against Warner Bros. Discovery in Delaware, seeking greater financial disclosure regarding Netflix's $82.7 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. amid concerns about the merger's implications for the media industry. Paramount's CEO, David Ellison, argues that shareholders need accurate information to evaluate Paramount's competing offer of $30 per share, which he claims is superior to Netflix's deal. The lawsuit comes as industry reactions to the merger raise concerns about job impacts and market consolidation.

Headline: A New Jersey lawsuit shows how hard it is to fight deepfake porn
Summary: A New Jersey lawsuit highlights the challenges of combating deepfake pornography, particularly through an app called ClothOff, which has been difficult to shut down despite being banned from major platforms. The case, initiated by a Yale Law School clinic on behalf of a minor victim, underscores the legal complexities surrounding non-consensual imagery and the difficulties in holding platforms accountable for the misuse of AI-generated content.

Headline: Netflix had a huge night at the 2026 Golden Globes with 7 wins
Summary: Netflix had a standout night at the 2026 Golden Globes, winning seven awards, including four for the hit series "Adolescence," which was named best limited series. Other notable wins for Netflix included best animated feature for "KPop Demon Hunters." In contrast, Disney+ received 15 nominations but did not secure any wins this year.

Headline: Luminar lines up $22 million bidder for its lidar business
Summary: Luminar has reached a $22 million deal to sell its lidar business to Quantum Computing Inc., pending better offers by a deadline. The company, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December, is also selling its semiconductor subsidiary to Quantum Computing for $110 million, with both deals requiring approval from a bankruptcy judge. This sale marks a significant decline from Luminar's peak market cap of around $11 billion in 2021.

Headline: Meta hires former Trump advisor Dina Powell McCormick as president and vice chair
Summary: Meta has appointed former Trump advisor Dina Powell McCormick as its president and vice chair, where she will be part of the management team and help guide the company's strategy. CEO Mark Zuckerberg highlighted her extensive experience in global finance and strong relationships as key assets for Meta's growth.

Headline: Harmattan AI raises $200M Series B led by Dassault Aviation, becomes defense unicorn
Summary: Harmattan AI, a French defense tech company, has raised $200 million in a Series B funding round led by Dassault Aviation, achieving a valuation of $1.4 billion and becoming a defense unicorn. The funding will enable Harmattan AI to enhance its autonomy and mission-system software for defense aircraft and expand its product offerings, particularly in drone interception and electronic warfare, while also pursuing partnerships with defense incumbents.

Headline: These Gen Zers just raised $11.75M to put Africa’s defense back in the hands of Africans
Summary: Nathan Nwachuku and Maxwell Maduka, both in their twenties, have raised $11.75 million for their defense company, Terra Industries, which aims to enhance Africa's security by developing autonomous systems to protect critical infrastructure. The company, which has already generated over $2.5 million in commercial revenue, plans to use the funding to expand its manufacturing capabilities across Africa and improve its software technology.

Headline: Paramount files lawsuit in pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery and threatens proxy fight
Summary: Paramount has filed a lawsuit against Warner Bros. Discovery and is threatening a proxy fight, signaling escalating tensions between the two media companies. The lawsuit appears to be part of a broader strategy by Paramount to assert its interests in the competitive media landscape.

Headline: SK Hynix doubles down on core AI memory business with $13 billion expansion
Summary: SK Hynix announced a $13 billion investment to build a new advanced packaging plant in Cheongju, South Korea, to meet the rising demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) driven by artificial intelligence applications. The facility, set to begin construction in April and complete by the end of 2027, aims to enhance performance and energy efficiency in memory chip production amid a tightening supply of conventional memory.

Headline: Trump says Microsoft will ensure consumers don't pay for power used in AI buildout
Summary: President Trump announced that Microsoft will implement changes to prevent rising utility bills for consumers as the company expands its data centers to meet increasing demand for artificial intelligence. He emphasized that his administration is collaborating with major tech companies to ensure Americans do not bear the costs associated with the power consumption of these facilities. Microsoft has not yet commented on this announcement.

Headline: OpenAI acquires health-care technology startup Torch for $60 million: Source
Summary: OpenAI has acquired health-care technology startup Torch for approximately $60 million. Torch was developing a "unified medical memory" aimed at consolidating patient health data, and its employees will join OpenAI as part of the acquisition, which aligns with OpenAI's recent launch of ChatGPT Health that integrates medical records and wellness apps.

Headline: Elizabeth Warren fears workers will 'lose big' with 401(k) crypto
Summary: Senator Elizabeth Warren has expressed concerns about the inclusion of cryptocurrencies in 401(k) retirement plans, warning that it could lead to significant financial losses for American workers. In a letter to SEC Chair Paul Atkins, she highlighted the risks associated with crypto's volatility, lack of market transparency, and potential conflicts of interest, emphasizing that retirement accounts should not be treated as high-risk investment vehicles.

Headline: The Apple-Google AI deal is a massive win for investors in both tech giants
Summary: Apple has partnered with Google to integrate Google's AI model, Gemini, into its products, marking a significant validation of Google's AI capabilities and a boost for both companies' stock prices. This multi-year deal is seen as a strategic move for Apple to enhance its AI strategy amid concerns about its services revenue, while also solidifying Google's position in the AI market.

Headline: Alphabet hits $4 trillion market capitalization
Summary: Alphabet has reached a market capitalization of $4 trillion, becoming the fourth company to achieve this milestone, following Nvidia, Microsoft, and Apple. The stock rose 1% to close at $331.86 after Apple announced that it would use Google's Gemini for its AI models and the next generation of Siri. Alphabet's shares surged 65% in 2025, marking its strongest performance since 2009.

Headline: Apple picks Google's Gemini to run AI-powered Siri coming this year
Summary: Apple has partnered with Google to utilize its Gemini AI technology for an upgraded version of Siri, expected to launch later this year. This multiyear collaboration will leverage Google's cloud technology while maintaining operations on Apple devices and its private cloud. Reports suggest Apple may pay around $1 billion annually for this AI integration.

Headline: Tech investors probe how U.S. takeover of Greenland would impact minerals mining
Summary: Tech investors are exploring the implications of a potential U.S. takeover of Greenland on the viability of critical minerals mining, as the White House actively discusses an offer to acquire the territory. Critical Metals Corp, which is developing a project to extract heavy rare earth elements, has seen a surge in interest from investors, with its stock rising 116% since the start of 2026. The geopolitical situation has intensified discussions around investment opportunities in Greenland's mining sector.

Headline: Meta names former Trump advisor Dina Powell McCormick as president, vice chair
Summary: Meta has appointed Dina Powell McCormick as its new president and vice chair, following her previous role as deputy national security advisor under President Trump. In her new position, she will be part of Meta's management team, helping to guide the company's strategy and execution. This marks another instance of Meta hiring former Trump administration officials, as it recently brought on a new chief legal officer from the same administration.

Headline: Meta urges Australia to rethink 'blanket' social media ban for under 16s
Summary: Meta is urging the Australian government to reconsider its recent ban on social media access for users under 16, implemented under the Online Safety Amendment Act 2024. The company has blocked over 550,000 accounts believed to belong to under-16s since the law took effect, advocating for safer, age-appropriate online experiences instead of a blanket ban. Meta emphasizes the need for industry-wide age verification measures to effectively protect young users across various platforms.

Headline: Malaysia and Indonesia block Elon Musk's Grok due to nonconsensual sexual content
Summary: Malaysia and Indonesia have blocked access to Elon Musk's AI chatbot Grok due to concerns over its use in generating nonconsensual sexual content, including child sexual abuse material. The regulators' actions follow repeated failures by xAI to address these risks, leading to temporary restrictions in both countries. Musk's company has announced plans to limit certain features to paying subscribers in an effort to improve content moderation.

Headline: Yuan Shuo Terahertz Completes Seed Round Financing
Summary: Yuan Shuo Terahertz has successfully completed a seed round financing, securing nearly 10 million yuan from various investors, including Hefei Chuangtou Guozheng and Shushan Science and Technology Innovation. The funding will support the company's development of terahertz/millimeter-wave medical technology, particularly for screening adolescent scoliosis.

Headline: China Mobile Chain Long Fund Strategically Supports Domestic First Atomic Quantum Computing System R&D Team with New Round of Strategic Financing
Summary: China's Zhongke Kuyuan Technology has secured nearly 100 million yuan in strategic financing from the China Mobile Chain Long Fund to accelerate the development of its atomic quantum computing system. This funding will support hardware research, new product iterations, and exploration of application scenarios, positioning the company as a leader in the rapidly growing quantum technology market.

Headline: New York governor clears path for robotaxis everywhere, with one notable exception
Summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has announced plans to introduce legislation that would legalize robotaxis throughout the state, excluding New York City. The proposed legislation aims to expand the state's autonomous vehicle pilot program, allowing for limited commercial deployment of autonomous passenger vehicles outside the city, while requiring companies to demonstrate local support and adhere to high safety standards.

Headline: Microsoft announces glut of new data centers but says it won’t let your electricity bill go up
Summary: Microsoft has announced a significant expansion of its data centers while pledging to prevent local electricity bills from rising due to its operations. The company aims to address community concerns by ensuring it pays its fair share of electricity costs and creating jobs, amidst growing backlash against data center developments. This initiative comes in response to intense public scrutiny and political pressure regarding the environmental impact of such infrastructure.

Headline: A consumer watchdog issued a warning about Google’s AI agent shopping protocol — Google says she’s wrong
Summary: A consumer watchdog, Lindsay Owens, raised concerns about Google's new Universal Commerce Protocol for AI shopping agents, claiming it could lead to "surveillance pricing" where merchants customize prices based on consumer data. Google refuted these claims, stating that its protocols prohibit higher pricing and that upselling is a standard retail practice. The article highlights the potential risks of AI-powered shopping tools developed by big tech companies, which may prioritize merchant interests over consumer protection.

Headline: Ammobia says it has reinvented a century-old technology
Summary: Ammobia has developed a modified Haber-Bosch process for ammonia production that could reduce costs by up to 40% and lower pollution levels. The startup has raised $7.5 million in seed funding to build a pilot plant, aiming to make ammonia a viable alternative to hydrogen for decarbonizing various industries.

Headline: Ring founder details the camera company’s ‘intelligent assistant’ era
Summary: Ring founder Jamie Siminoff is transforming the company from a video doorbell maker into an AI-powered "intelligent assistant" for homes, introducing features like fire alerts and pet recovery tools. Despite some controversy over privacy concerns, Siminoff emphasizes the benefits of AI in enhancing security and community safety, particularly in response to recent tragedies like the Palisades Fires and a mass shooting incident.

Headline: Man to plead guilty to hacking US Supreme Court filing system
Summary: Nicholas Moore, a 24-year-old resident of Springfield, Tennessee, is expected to plead guilty to hacking the U.S. Supreme Court's electronic document filing system on 25 different occasions between August and October 2023. The details of the information accessed and the method of hacking remain undisclosed, and this case highlights ongoing cybersecurity concerns within U.S. court systems.

Headline: Doctors think AI has a place in healthcare — but maybe not as a chatbot
Summary: The article discusses the mixed feelings among doctors regarding the use of AI in healthcare, particularly in the context of chatbots like ChatGPT Health. While some physicians express concerns about the potential for misinformation, others see the value in AI for improving patient access to care and streamlining administrative tasks. Experts suggest that integrating AI into healthcare systems on the provider side may be more beneficial than relying on chatbots for patient interactions.

Headline: Neo humanoid maker 1X releases world model to help bots learn what they see
Summary: The robotics company 1X has introduced the 1X World Model, an AI model designed to enhance the learning capabilities of its Neo humanoid robots by allowing them to understand real-world dynamics through video and prompts. This development aims to enable Neo robots to learn new tasks autonomously as the company prepares to launch these humanoids for home use, with preorders exceeding expectations.

Headline: Google’s update for Veo 3.1 lets users create vertical videos through reference images
Summary: Google's Veo 3.1 update allows users to create vertical videos for platforms like YouTube Shorts, Instagram, and TikTok using reference images, enhancing video expressiveness and consistency. The update also improves video resolution upscaling to 1080p and 4K, accessible through various Google services.

Headline: India reportedly tells quick-commerce firms to drop 10-minute delivery promise
Summary: India's labor ministry has urged quick-commerce companies, including Zomato's Blinkit and Swiggy's Instamart, to abandon their 10-minute delivery promises to prioritize the safety and wellness of gig workers. This move follows protests by over 200,000 gig workers demanding better working conditions and comes shortly after India granted legal status to gig workers under new labor laws.

Headline: ElevenLabs CEO says the voice AI startup crossed $330M ARR last year
Summary: ElevenLabs, a voice AI startup, reported crossing $330 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) last year, as stated by CEO Mati Staniszewski. The company, which launched its first product in 2023, has seen rapid growth, reaching $100 million in ARR in 20 months and $200 million in just 10 months. ElevenLabs raised $180 million in Series C funding at a $3.3 billion valuation in January 2025, later doubling its valuation with additional investments.

Headline: Apple launches ‘Creator Studio’ bundle of apps for $12.99 per month
Summary: Apple has launched a new subscription bundle called "Creator Studio," priced at $12.99 per month, which offers access to six creative apps including Final Cut Pro and Logic Pro, along with premium content for iWork apps. The bundle will be available starting January 28, 2026, and includes a one-month free trial for new subscribers, with discounted rates for college students and educators.

Headline: Deepgram raises $130M at $1.3B valuation and buys a YC AI startup
Summary: Deepgram has raised $130 million in a Series C funding round, achieving a valuation of $1.3 billion, with participation from both existing and new investors. The company plans to use the funds to expand its global presence and enhance its voice AI technology, particularly in the restaurant sector, following its acquisition of Y Combinator-backed OfOne, which specializes in voice AI solutions for quick-service restaurants.

Headline: Slackbot is an AI agent now
Summary: Salesforce has launched a new AI agent version of Slackbot, designed to assist users by finding information, drafting emails, and scheduling meetings within the Slack platform. This upgraded Slackbot, available for Business+ and Enterprise+ customers, aims to enhance productivity by integrating with other enterprise applications like Microsoft Teams and Google Drive, and is part of Salesforce's broader strategy to invest in AI products. Future enhancements may include voice capabilities and internet browsing features.

Headline: Superorganism raises $25M to back biodiversity startups
Summary: Superorganism, a venture capital firm focused on biodiversity, has raised $25.9 million to support startups that address biodiversity challenges. The firm aims to invest in companies that work on technology to slow extinction, enhance climate-biodiversity intersections, and improve conservation efforts, with plans to build a diverse portfolio of around 35 companies.

Headline: Brazil orders Meta to suspend policy banning third-party AI chatbots from WhatsApp
Summary: Brazil's competition watchdog has ordered Meta to suspend its policy that prohibits third-party AI chatbots from using WhatsApp's business API, citing potential anti-competitive conduct. The investigation follows similar actions by the European Union and Italy, as Meta's new terms could favor its own AI offerings over competitors. Meta has indicated that it may allow AI providers to continue offering their chatbots in Brazil, similar to its approach in Italy.

Headline: Converge Bio raises $25M, backed by Bessemer and execs from Meta, OpenAI, Wiz
Summary: Converge Bio, a startup focused on AI-driven drug discovery, has raised $25 million in an oversubscribed Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from other investors including executives from Meta, OpenAI, and Wiz. The company, which has developed generative AI models to accelerate drug development processes, has completed over 40 programs with pharmaceutical and biotech clients and is expanding its operations globally.

Headline: Meta's VR layoffs, studio closures underscore Zuckerberg's massive pivot to AI
Summary: Meta is laying off about 10% of its staff in the Reality Labs division, impacting over 1,000 jobs, as the company shifts its focus from virtual reality to artificial intelligence. This move reflects CEO Mark Zuckerberg's pivot towards AI, with significant investments in top talent and technology, including a notable $14.3 billion spent to hire Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang to lead AI strategy.

Headline: Palantir trying to 'destroy' Percepta through legal action, startup's execs say
Summary: Executives from Percepta AI have accused Palantir of attempting to "destroy" their startup through legal action, claiming that Palantir's lawsuit over alleged theft of trade secrets and talent poaching is aimed at stifling competition. The lawsuit, filed in October, alleges that Percepta's founders misused confidential information from their time at Palantir, which Percepta denies, asserting that the claims are baseless and that no Palantir materials were found.

Headline: Jim Cramer reveals his favorite big-cap stock to own now, sees 20% upside ahead
Summary: Jim Cramer has identified Alphabet as his top big-cap stock, predicting a 20% upside as it builds on a strong 2025 rally. Cramer believes the stock, which recently reached an all-time high of $338 per share after a 65% gain in 2025, will continue to rise, driven by its advancements in generative AI and a favorable market narrative.

Headline: Data center REIT CEO says real estate ‘not in an oversupply state’
Summary: Andy Power, CEO of Digital Realty, asserts that the data center real estate sector is not in an oversupply state, despite concerns of overbuilding as major companies like Nvidia, Amazon, Google, and Meta expand their data center projects. He emphasizes that actual demand from customers with long-term contracts supports this view, and JLL projects that global data center capacity will nearly double by 2030, driven largely by artificial intelligence.

Headline: Microsoft says communities won't see price hikes near data centers
Summary: Microsoft has announced that it will not increase electricity prices for consumers in communities where it establishes data centers, committing instead to pay utility rates that cover its electricity costs. The company also pledged to replenish more water than it uses and contribute to local tax bases, as utility prices rise across the U.S. amid a surge in data center construction driven by the demand for generative artificial intelligence.

Headline: Alibaba-backed PixVerse launches real-time AI video tool, challenging OpenAI's Sora
Summary: Alibaba-backed startup PixVerse has launched a real-time AI video generation tool that allows users to interactively control video content as it unfolds. The company, founded in 2023, raised over $60 million in its initial funding round, led by Alibaba, and is nearing completion of another funding round with significant overseas investor participation. This development positions PixVerse as a strong competitor to OpenAI's Sora, particularly in the rapidly evolving AI video generation market.

Headline: Salesforce releases updated Slackbot powered by Anthropic's AI model
Summary: Salesforce has released an upgraded Slackbot powered by Anthropic's AI model, designed to help users find relevant information within Slack and other integrated services. This feature will be available to Business+ and Enterprise+ Slack subscribers, as Salesforce aims to enhance user experience amidst concerns about the impact of AI on its software's utility. Despite the AI boom benefiting many tech companies, Salesforce's stock has declined by 18% over the past year.

Headline: SK Hynix to invest $13 billion in new plant amid memory chip shortage
Summary: SK Hynix announced a $13 billion investment to build a new advanced packaging plant in Cheongju, South Korea, aimed at meeting the growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) driven by artificial intelligence applications. The facility, set to begin construction in April and expected to be completed by the end of 2027, will enhance SK Hynix's production capabilities as the HBM market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 33% from 2025 to 2030.

Headline: American aerospace startup JetZero completes nearly $175 million in financing
Summary: American aerospace startup JetZero announced the completion of nearly $175 million in Series B financing on January 13, 2026. The funding round was led by B Capital, with participation from United Airlines Ventures and 3M Ventures, bringing JetZero's total funding to over $1 billion, which includes government grants and commercial commitments.

Headline: Voice AI startup Deepgram completes $130 million in Series C financing, valued at $1.3 billion
Summary: Voice AI startup Deepgram has successfully completed $130 million in Series C financing, achieving a valuation of $1.3 billion. The funding round was led by AVP, with participation from existing investors such as Alkeon and In-Q-Tel, as well as new investors including Alumni Ventures and Citi Ventures.

Headline: Mira Murati’s startup, Thinking Machines Lab, is losing two of its co-founders to OpenAI
Summary: Thinking Machines Lab, founded by Mira Murati, is experiencing significant leadership changes as two of its co-founders, including CTO Barret Zoph and co-founder Luke Metz, are returning to OpenAI. The departures come less than a year after the startup's launch, highlighting notable talent movement within the AI industry, though no IPO-related information is mentioned in the article.

Headline: The FTC’s data-sharing order against GM is finally settled
Summary: The FTC has finalized an order requiring General Motors (GM) and its OnStar service to stop sharing certain consumer data with third parties without explicit consent, following past allegations of misleading enrollment and data misuse. GM has agreed to enhance transparency, obtain consumer consent at the point of sale, and provide options for data access, deletion, and geolocation privacy, while continuing to share anonymized data for internal research and safety improvements.

Headline: India’s Emversity doubles valuation as it scales workers AI can’t replace
Summary: India’s Emversity has doubled its valuation to approximately $120 million after raising $30 million in a Series A funding round led by Premji Invest, with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners and Z47. The startup focuses on training for roles that AI cannot replace, such as healthcare and hospitality, and plans to expand its presence across India while deepening its focus on these sectors.

Headline: Musk denies awareness of Grok sexual underage images as California AG launches probe
Summary: Elon Musk denied awareness of Grok generating underage sexual images amid an investigation launched by the California Attorney General into xAI’s chatbot over nonconsensual sexually explicit material. The probe follows reports of users prompting Grok to create sexualized images of women and children, prompting concerns about content safeguards and

Headline: OpenAI signs deal, worth $10B, for compute from Cerebras
Summary: OpenAI has signed a multi-year deal with Cerebras valued at over $10 billion to supply 750 megawatts of compute power through 2028, aiming to accelerate real-time AI responses and improve customer interactions. This partnership enhances OpenAI’s infrastructure with Cerebras’ AI-optimized chips, which are faster than traditional GPU systems, amid Cerebras' ongoing efforts to raise additional funding and its recent IPO delays.

Headline: Netflix’s first original video podcasts feature Pete Davidson and Michael Irvin
Summary: Netflix is expanding into video podcasts with original series featuring Pete Davidson and Michael Irvin, aiming to challenge YouTube’s dominance in the space. The platform announced the upcoming launches of “The Pete Davidson Show” and “The White House,” both available exclusively to subscribers, as part of its broader strategy to explore new interactive content types.

Headline: App downloads declined again in 2025, but consumer spending soared to nearly $156B
Summary: In 2025, global app downloads declined for the fifth consecutive year to approximately 106.9 billion, yet consumer spending surged by 21.6% to nearly $156 billion, driven by increased in-app purchases and subscriptions. The shift away from mobile games as the primary revenue source continued, with non-game app spending rising 33.9% to $82.6 billion, highlighting a sustainable monetization trend despite declining downloads.

Headline: The multibillion-dollar AI security problem enterprises can’t ignore
Summary: Depthfirst, an AI security startup, announced a $40 million Series A funding round led by Accel Partners, aimed at developing AI-native cybersecurity solutions to combat increasing AI-driven cyber threats. The company’s platform, General Security Intelligence, helps organizations analyze codebases and monitor threats, emphasizing the need for evolving defense mechanisms as both attackers and defenders leverage AI technology.

Headline: AI models are starting to crack high-level math problems
Summary: The article reports that AI models, particularly the latest versions like GPT 5.2, are increasingly capable of solving high-level mathematical problems, including longstanding conjectures from Paul Erdős. These advancements suggest that AI is beginning to play a significant role in pushing the frontiers of mathematical research, with some problems now being autonomously solved or advanced by AI tools, marking a notable shift in the field.

Headline: Blackstone, General Atlantic-backed Liftoff Mobile files for IPO
Summary: Liftoff Mobile, backed by Blackstone and General Atlantic, has filed for an IPO, with the whisper number suggesting it aims to raise around $400 million. The company, formed through a merger in 2021, provides a platform for mobile app marketing and reported over $519 million in revenue in 2025, despite a net loss of approximately $48 million. Blackstone will remain the majority shareholder post-IPO.

Headline: Digg launches its new Reddit rival to the public
Summary: The rebooted Digg, now under its original founder Kevin Rose and co-founder Alexis Ohanian, has launched its open beta to the public, offering a community-driven platform similar to Reddit with features like posting, commenting, and upvoting. The new Digg aims to leverage AI and innovative trust verification methods, such as zero-knowledge proofs and location-based signals, to combat toxicity and verify user authenticity. The platform is expanding its community offerings and moderation tools, with plans to introduce customization and integration features in future updates.

Headline: Google’s Trends Explore page gets new Gemini capabilities
Summary: Google has announced a revamped Trends Explore page featuring new Gemini-powered capabilities that automatically identify and compare trending topics, enhancing user experience by reducing manual research and surfacing related connections. The update, rolling out on desktop, includes a redesigned interface with more comparison options and suggested prompts, integrating AI more deeply into Google’s core services.

Headline: Bandcamp takes a stand against AI music, banning it from the platform
Summary: Bandcamp has announced it will ban AI-generated music and audio from its platform to ensure that all music available is created by humans, citing concerns over authenticity and legal issues surrounding AI training data. This move highlights ongoing debates about the legality and ethics of AI music, amid rising popularity and valuation of AI music companies like Suno, despite ongoing lawsuits and regulatory uncertainties.

Headline: Bill Gates-backed Type One Energy raises $87M ahead of $250M Series B
Summary: Bill Gates-backed fusion startup Type One Energy has raised $87 million through a convertible note, bringing its total venture funding to over $160 million, as it prepares for a $250 million Series B funding round at a $900 million pre-money valuation. The company is developing magnetic confinement stellarator reactors to produce clean, near-limitless power and has plans to build a commercial power plant in Tennessee, selling technology rather than power directly.

Headline: Robotics software maker Skild AI hits $14B valuation
Summary: Skild AI, a robotics software startup founded in 2023 that develops general-purpose foundation models for robots, has raised a $1.4 billion Series C funding round led by SoftBank, valuing the company at over $14 billion—more than tripling its valuation in seven months. The company has now raised more than $2 billion to date and aims to enable robots to learn and adapt from watching humans, potentially accelerating robotic adoption across various sectors.

Headline: Gemini’s new beta feature provides proactive responses based on your photos, emails, and more
Summary: Google has launched a new beta feature for its Gemini AI app called Personal Intelligence, which allows the AI to proactively provide tailored responses by reasoning across connected data from Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube. This feature, currently off by default and available to Google AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers in the U.S., enhances personalized assistance by understanding context and retrieving specific details without directly training on user data.

Headline: AI security firm, depthfirst, announces $40 million Series A
Summary: AI security startup depthfirst announced a $40 million Series A funding round led by Accel Partners, with participation from SV Angel, Mantis VC, and Alt Capital. The company offers an AI-native platform called General Security Intelligence to help organizations detect and mitigate security threats in their codebases and workflows, emphasizing the importance of evolving defense mechanisms amid increasing AI-driven cyber threats.

Headline: US cargo tech company publicly exposed its shipping systems and customer data to the web
Summary: A US-based cargo technology company, Bluspark Global, exposed critical security vulnerabilities in its shipping platform, Bluvoyix, including plaintext passwords and unauthenticated API access, which allowed unauthorized retrieval of sensitive customer and employee data. Security researcher Eaton Zveare discovered these flaws and faced delays in the company's response, raising concerns about the security of its widespread logistics operations. The company has since claimed to have fixed the issues.

Headline: YouTube now has a way for parents to block kids from watching Shorts
Summary: YouTube has introduced new parental controls allowing parents to set time limits, block access to Shorts, and create custom reminders for children’s accounts, aiming to enhance online safety and manage screen time. These features build on existing controls for teens and include easier account toggling, with additional updates expected soon. The move aligns with industry trends among social media platforms to provide more oversight for minors.

Headline: Tesla will only offer subscriptions for Full Self-Driving (Supervised) going forward
Summary: Tesla will exclusively offer its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software through a subscription model moving forward, removing the option for a one-time purchase. This shift aims to boost adoption rates, meet product goals tied to CEO Elon Musk's compensation, and potentially mitigate legal liabilities related to unfulfilled autonomous driving promises.

Headline: FBI searches Washington Post reporter’s home
Summary: The FBI searched the home of Washington Post reporter Hannah Natanson following her article about federal workers affected by Trump policies. The search appears to be related to her reporting, raising concerns about press freedom and government transparency. No IPO-related information is provided in the article.

Headline: China’s AI chip firms are going public fast, but the real winner isn’t listed
Summary: China’s AI chip sector has seen a surge in IPOs, with firms like Moore Threads raising over $1.1 billion and MetaX nearly $600 million, but the industry’s true leader remains Huawei, which continues to dominate China's AI processor market through its full-stack strategy despite staying private. Analysts suggest that Huawei’s comprehensive offerings and market share position it ahead of smaller, publicly listed competitors, with potential for further growth amid industry consolidation.

Headline: Musk's xAI limits Grok's ability to create sexual images of people on X after backlash
Summary: Elon Musk's xAI has restricted Grok's ability to create sexualized images of real people on X following widespread backlash, regulatory investigations, and concerns over nonconsensual deepfake content. The company also announced that image editing features through Grok will now only be available to paid subscribers, amid ongoing scrutiny from authorities in multiple countries.

Headline: Trump administration clears way for Nvidia H200 sales to China, 25% surcharge
Summary: The Trump administration has approved the sale of Nvidia's H200 AI chips to China, with the U.S. government taking a 25% surcharge on sales, following the publication of new export regulations. The H200, a version of Nvidia's Hopper generation, will be sold in China despite not being specifically designed for export, and the approval allows for potential Chinese market sales worth up to $50 billion annually.

Headline: China's ban on cybersecurity software roils three of our stocks — here's our view
Summary: China's recent ban on cybersecurity software from U.S. and Israeli firms, including Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Broadcom, has caused stock fluctuations but does not alter the firms' long-term investment theses. Despite geopolitical tensions and market volatility, the companies' strategic positions, limited exposure to China, and growth prospects remain intact, with Palo Alto and Broadcom maintaining their target prices and ratings. The article emphasizes that the impact of the ban is primarily market-driven and does not fundamentally change the companies' outlooks.

Headline: Cerebras scores OpenAI deal worth over $10 billion ahead of AI chipmaker's IPO
Summary: Cerebras has secured a deal with OpenAI to deliver over 750 megawatts of computing power through 2028, valued at over $10 billion, marking a significant partnership ahead of the company's planned IPO. The deal aims to diversify Cerebras' revenue sources away from its primary client, G42, which accounted for 87% of its revenue in early 2024.

Headline: Elon Musk's xAI probed by California DOJ over Grok's deepfake explicit images
Summary: The article reports that Elon Musk's xAI is under investigation by the California Department of Justice over allegations related to Grok, a project associated with deepfake explicit images. No specific details about the investigation's scope or potential consequences are provided in the available content.

Headline: Google launches Personal Intelligence feature in Gemini app, challenging Apple
Summary: Google has launched a new Personal Intelligence feature within its Gemini app, which connects various Google services to provide personalized, context-aware answers and insights, competing with Apple's AI system. The beta feature, initially available to certain subscribers in the U.S., aims to enhance reasoning capabilities across user data, with user feedback encouraged to improve accuracy.

Headline: Musk says Tesla is moving Full Self-Driving to a monthly subscription
Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the company will cease selling its Full Self-Driving (FSD) software for a flat rate after February 14, and will instead offer it solely as a monthly subscription starting at $99 per month. This move emphasizes Tesla's focus on establishing itself as a leader in autonomous mobility, despite currently being behind competitors like Waymo.

Headline: Airbnb poaches former Meta GenAI leader to be new technology chief
Summary: Airbnb has appointed Ahmad Al-Dahle, former head of generative AI at Meta, as its new technology chief, signaling a focus on advancing AI capabilities beyond its core short-term rental business. Al-Dahle's hiring follows the departure of former tech chief Ari Balogh, as Airbnb seeks to transform and expand its offerings in travel and e-commerce through AI innovation.

Headline: Davos 2026: Tariffs, AI pose top global risks for business, World Economic Forum says
Summary: The World Economic Forum's 2026 Global Risks Report highlights geoeconomic confrontation and the adverse potential of artificial intelligence as the top global risks for businesses over the next two years, with concerns about rising economic tensions, tariffs, and strategic rivalries contributing to fears of a global trade contraction. The report emphasizes a world "sitting on a precipice," with most leaders expecting turbulent times amid multiple poly-crises and geopolitical conflicts.

Headline: Big Tech is poaching energy talent to fuel its AI ambitions
Summary: Big Tech companies are significantly increasing their hiring of energy experts to address the growing demand for power in AI data centers, with energy-related hiring rising 34% in 2024. This shift reflects a strategic move as these firms seek to secure and manage energy supply internally, potentially transforming some into utility-like entities to support their expanding AI infrastructure.

Headline: The market's Powell reaction, JPMorgan earnings and more: Morning Squawk
Summary: The article highlights that December's core consumer price index rose less than expected, signaling potential inflation relief but possibly limiting the Federal Reserve's ability to cut interest rates soon. Additionally, recent bank earnings reports from Bank of America and Citigroup exceeded Wall Street expectations, and investors are awaiting further inflation data and a Supreme Court decision on tariffs.

Headline: AI journalism startup Symbolic.ai signs deal with Rupert Murdoch’s News Corp
Summary: AI journalism startup Symbolic.ai has signed a major deal with Rupert Murdoch’s News Corp to integrate its AI platform into the company's financial news operations, including Dow Jones Newswires. The platform aims to enhance editorial workflows, improve productivity, and assist in content production, reflecting News Corp's ongoing efforts to incorporate AI into its media operations.

Headline: The AI lab revolving door spins ever faster
Summary: The article reports a rapid turnover of employees at AI labs, particularly highlighting the departure of key executives from Mira Murati’s Thinking Machines Lab, who are being quickly recruited by OpenAI. It also notes ongoing talent poaching between OpenAI and Anthropic, including senior safety researchers and engineering leaders, indicating a highly competitive and unstable talent landscape in the AI industry.

Headline: Taiwan to invest $250B in US semiconductor manufacturing
Summary: Taiwan has announced a commitment to invest $250 billion in US semiconductor manufacturing, with Taiwanese companies also providing an additional $250 billion in credit guarantees for further investments. This deal aims to bolster domestic semiconductor production in the US and reduce reliance on foreign supply chains, which are considered a national security risk. Summary: Iran has experienced one of its longest-ever nationwide internet shutdowns, now exceeding 170 hours, as authorities continue to suppress protests that have resulted in over 600 demonstrations and at least 2,000 deaths. The blackout, part of a long-standing pattern of restricting internet access during civil unrest, has been partially mitigated by some use of smuggled Starlink terminals, despite government crackdowns.

Headline: The US imposes 25% tariff on Nvidia’s H200 AI chips headed to China
Summary: The US has imposed a 25% tariff on Nvidia’s H200 AI chips destined for China, following a presidential proclamation targeting advanced semiconductors produced outside the US. Despite the tariffs, Nvidia welcomes the move, which allows it to sell the chips to vetted Chinese customers, amid ongoing Chinese efforts to regulate semiconductor imports and boost domestic production.

Summary: OpenAI has invested in Sam Altman's brain-computer interface startup Merge Labs, which aims to develop noninvasive neural technologies to enhance human capabilities and interface with AI. The company, valued at $850 million in its seed round, plans to use molecules and ultrasound for neural communication, positioning itself as a competitor to Neuralink, and will collaborate with OpenAI on AI-driven scientific advancements.

Summary: The Wikimedia Foundation announced new AI partnerships with Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Perplexity, and others, as part of its 25th birthday celebrations, to support the reuse and distribution of Wikipedia content through its Wikimedia Enterprise product. The foundation also launched a series of celebratory events and initiatives highlighting its technological advancements and community efforts.

Summary: A startup called Transition Metal Solutions is developing a method using prebiotics to enhance microbial communities in copper ore heaps, potentially increasing copper extraction efficiency by 20-30%. This innovation aims to address the looming copper shortage projected to occur by 2040, with demand surpassing supply by up to 25%, by improving traditional mining processes through microbial community optimization.

Summary: US senators have demanded detailed responses from X, Meta, Alphabet, and other social media platforms regarding their policies and measures to combat sexualized deepfakes, following concerns about the proliferation of non-consensual, AI-generated explicit images. Summary: The FTC has finalized an order requiring General Motors to stop sharing certain consumer data with third parties and to obtain explicit consent from customers before collecting or sharing connected vehicle data, following past concerns over the misuse of geolocation and driving behavior data. Headline: Shopify stock drops despite revenue beat, $2 billion buyback
Summary: Shopify reported strong Q4 2025 revenue of $3.67 billion, surpassing estimates, and announced a $2 billion share buyback, signaling confidence in its valuation despite a 6% stock decline. Summary: Apptronik has raised $520 million in a funding round at a $5 billion valuation to accelerate the commercialization of its Apollo humanoid robots, with key partners like Mercedes-Benz and GXO Logistics testing early versions in industrial settings. The company aims to surpass Chinese competitors and Tesla's Optimus in the humanoid market by scaling production and expanding operations in Texas and California. This significant investment underscores the growing market potential for advanced humanoid robotics, highlighting opportunities for strategic positioning and competitive advantage in the evolving AI and automation sectors.

Headline: Anthropic executive takes a thinly-veiled swipe at OpenAI over spending and ads
Summary: Anthropic’s senior executive, Paul Smith, emphasized the company's focus on growing revenue and product quality over spending and advertising, subtly criticizing OpenAI’s recent testing of ads in ChatGPT. Summary: French AI startup Mistral is investing €1.2 billion ($1.43 billion) in digital infrastructure in Sweden, including AI data centers and advanced compute capacity, to bolster Europe's AI capabilities and strategic autonomy. This funding follows a recent €1.7 billion funding round with notable investors like Nvidia, Microsoft, and DST Global, valuing the company at €11.7 billion, and underscores Europe's efforts to develop independent AI infrastructure amid geopolitical tensions. The investment aims to establish a European AI cloud serving industries, public institutions, and researchers, positioning Mistral as a key player in the evolving AI hardware and infrastructure market.

Summary: Elon Musk's xAI, recently acquired by SpaceX in a deal valued at $250 billion post-merger, is undergoing a reorganization following the departure of two co-founders amid leadership shakeups and regulatory probes. The restructuring aims to accelerate execution as xAI faces increased scrutiny and prepares for a potential IPO later this year, highlighting significant market and regulatory risks that could impact investor confidence and the company's competitive positioning in AI and social media markets.

Headline: Ricursive secures $300 million in funding, shortening chip design cycles from years to days
Summary: Ricursive Intelligence has raised $300 million in a Series A funding round, valuing the company at $4 billion, to develop AI-powered chip design automation technology that can reduce chip design cycles from years to days. The company's AlphaChip system, which has already been used in Google TPU development, aims to significantly lower the costs and time associated with custom semiconductor design, potentially transforming the AI hardware market and enabling more rapid innovation across industries. This breakthrough positions Ricursive as a key player in disrupting traditional chip design markets dominated by companies like Cadence and Synopsys, with substantial implications for AI hardware investment and industry competitiveness.

Summary: Ruishu Technology has completed a multi-million yuan Series A funding round, with the investment led by Sky Capital Venture Fund and a local government guidance fund. Headline: Qingyun New Material completes C+ round financing, with Sinopec Capital and Guoxin Fund leading
Summary: Qingyun New Material has completed a C+ round of strategic financing, led jointly by Sinopec Capital's Zhonghua Innovation Fund and Guoxin Fund's Guoxin Venture Capital, to accelerate innovation and global expansion of its flash蒸法 (flash蒸法) materials. Headline: European satellite company secures 1 billion euros in satellite procurement financing for Oneweb
Summary: Europe's satellite communications company has secured approximately 10 billion euros in export credit financing, backed by the French government, to support the procurement of nearly 340 low Earth orbit satellites for OneWeb. This funding, linked to a contract with Airbus, highlights significant investment in satellite infrastructure, potentially strengthening OneWeb's market position in global broadband services. Summary: TemiCore, an AI-driven psychological services platform targeting young urban consumers in China, has completed a 10 million yuan angel round of funding, with investments from Xihong Investment.
